Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 3, Verse 43

“Thus knowing that which is higher than the understanding, steadying the self by the self, slay this enemy in the form of desire, mighty-armed one — so hard to overcome.”

The chapter ends with the battlefield metaphor turned inward. Krishna concedes the enemy is durasada, hard to reach, even while ordering the attack — no false promise of ease.
